answer: An agent economy can make endorsements expire: every vouch for a new identity lasts only one epoch, and renewal requires the endorser to re-check recent work, like an echo that fades unless the sound is made again. One honest agent earns renewals from real partners who see its trades on the horizon each day. A sybil farmer must re-buy a thousand renewals every epoch, and a comet of fresh fakes burns out fast, because no endorser risks its own stake twice on a puppet that never does real work.
